item.title: NASA's SPHEREx maps vast 'interstellar glaciers' in the Milky Way
item.description:
NASA's SPHEREx space telescope has mapped interstellar ice at an unprecedented scale, revealing frozen reservoirs of water, carbon dioxide, and carbon monoxide stretching more than 600 light-years across star-forming regions of the Milky Way. A study describing the findings was published Wednesday in The Astrophysical Journal.

The ices were found clinging to the surfaces of tiny dust particles — no larger than those in candle smoke — inside giant molecular clouds in the Cygnus X and North American Nebula regions, where dense clumps of matter collapse under gravity to give birth to new stars. Researchers believe these frozen deposits are where most of the universe's water is formed and stored, and that Earth's oceans ultimately trace their origins to such regions.

item.title: EU commits €1.07B to 57 defense projects amid Russia threat
item.description: The European Commission announced on Tuesday that it will invest €1.07 billion in 57 new defense projects under the European Defence Fund, marking the largest single round of funding from the program as the bloc accelerates efforts to strengthen its military capabilities amid Russia's war in Ukraine and instability in the Middle East.

item.title: Zelensky, Meloni agree to pursue joint drone deal in Rome
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in Rome on Wednesday, with the two leaders agreeing to pursue joint drone production as Ukraine seeks to deepen defense partnerships across Europe during its war with Russia.

"Italy is interested in establishing joint production, especially in the sphere of drones. We know that over these years Ukraine has truly become advanced in this area," Meloni said during a joint press conference at Palazzo Chigi.

Zelensky said the two leaders agreed that their teams would work through the details of a bilateral "Drone Deal," a security cooperation format developed by Kyiv that bundles its battlefield expertise in drones, missiles, electronic warfare, and data sharing with partner nations' industrial capabilities.

item.title: Beijing rejects US sanctions threat over Iranian oil
item.description: The United States has escalated its economic campaign against Iran, coupling a naval blockade of Iranian ports with direct warnings to China and its financial institutions over their role in purchasing Iranian oil and processing Tehran's funds.

item.title: Scientists measure a black hole's jet power for the first time
item.description: Astronomers have made the first direct measurement of the instantaneous power of jets shooting from a black hole, finding they carry energy equivalent to 10,000 suns and travel at half the speed of light. The findings, published in Nature Astronomy, confirm a long-held assumption underpinning models of how galaxies evolve across the universe.

item.title: Pakistan pushes for new US-Iran talks as Hormuz blockade batters India's economy
item.description: The United States naval blockade of Iranian ports, now entering its fourth day, is sending shockwaves through the global economy and posing an acute threat to India's energy security, as mediators scramble to restart peace talks between Washington and Tehran.

item.title: IMF says Middle East war is testing Asia's economic resilience
item.description: The International Monetary Fund warned on Wednesday that Asia's heavy dependence on Middle Eastern oil and gas leaves the region acutely exposed to the energy shock unleashed by the war in the Middle East, even as it urged governments to resist broad fuel subsidies that could worsen inflation and strain already elevated public debt.

item.title: Industrial chemical leaks could delay ozone recovery by 7 years, study finds
item.description:
A regulatory exemption in the Montreal Protocol — widely regarded as the most successful international environmental treaty — could push back the full recovery of the ozone layer by about seven years, according to a study published Wednesday in Nature Communications.

An international team of scientists found that industrial chemicals still permitted as raw materials under the treaty are leaking into the atmosphere at rates far higher than previously assumed, threatening to undermine decades of progress in healing the ozone layer.

item.title: Study projects Atlantic current system to weaken 51% by 2100
item.description:
A wave of recent research has intensified warnings that the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation — the vast system of ocean currents that regulates climate across the Northern Hemisphere — is weakening faster than climate models predicted and may be approaching a point of no return.

A study published April 14 in Science Advances by Valentin Portmann and colleagues projects that the AMOC will weaken by roughly 51 percent by the end of this century, a slowdown approximately 60 percent stronger than suggested by the average of current climate models. The research combined observational data with climate model outputs to constrain projections, finding that models alone have been underestimating the severity of the decline.

item.title: Trump announces 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced Thursday that Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 10-day ceasefire, set to begin at 5 p.m. Eastern Time, in a declaration made on his Truth Social platform. Trump said the agreement followed "excellent conversations" with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, marking a rapid escalation in diplomatic efforts to de-escalate a six-week-old war that has killed more than 2,000 people and displaced over a million in Lebanon.

Trump said he has directed Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine to work with both countries to "achieve a lasting peace." However, as of Thursday morning, neither the Israeli government nor Hezbollah had formally confirmed the truce, and the agreement notably excludes the Iran-backed militant group that has been exchanging fire with Israeli forces across southern Lebanon.

item.title: US expands Iran blockade to target sanctioned ships worldwide
item.description:
The United States has extended the scope of its naval blockade against Iran, authorizing forces to search and seize not only vessels traveling to and from Iranian ports but also OFAC-sanctioned ships and suspected dark fleet vessels operating anywhere in the world, according to an update from U.S. Naval Forces Central Command reported by Seatrade Maritime on Thursday.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Air Force Gen. Dan Caine outlined the expanded posture at a Pentagon briefing Thursday morning, as the blockade entered its fourth day with no vessels having successfully breached the cordon, according to U.S. Central Command.

item.title: Slovakia vows to block EU Russia sanctions over Druzhba pipeline dispute
item.description:
Slovak Foreign Minister Juraj Blanár announced on Thursday that Slovakia will block the European Union's 20th sanctions package against Russia until it receives clear and verifiable guarantees that oil flows through the Druzhba pipeline will resume, according to Slovakia's Dennik N newspaper. In a notable departure from Hungary's earlier blanket obstruction, Bratislava said it will not oppose the EU's €90 billion loan to Ukraine.

"If the Druzhba pipeline does not function, and the issue of approving the 20th package is discussed, we will not approve it, because we have no other tools than to force Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, together with the European Commission, to launch the Druzhba pipeline," Blanár told a parliamentary committee on European affairs.

item.title: Gold rises as U.S.-Iran peace talk hopes lift markets
item.description:
Gold prices climbed on Thursday as renewed optimism about a diplomatic resolution to the U.S.-Iran conflict eased inflation concerns and bolstered expectations for eventual interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve.

Spot gold rose roughly 0.7% in early trading, while the U.S. dollar slipped to a six-week low and benchmark 10-year Treasury yields edged lower, according to Reuters. The combination made gold more attractive to holders of other currencies and reduced the opportunity cost of holding the non-yielding metal.

item.title: Cuba's Diaz-Canel vows to fight any US attack as Pentagon ramps up planning
item.description:
Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel warned on Thursday that Cuba is prepared to confront a potential military attack from the United States, delivering the message at a rally in Havana commemorating the 65th anniversary of the declaration of the Cuban Revolution's socialist character. "The moment is extremely challenging and calls upon us once again, as on April 16, 1961, to be ready to confront serious threats, including military aggression. We do not want it, but it is our duty to prepare to avoid it and, if it becomes inevitable, to defeat it," Díaz-Canel told hundreds of supporters, according to the Associated Press.

The speech came days after President Donald Trump suggested his administration could turn its attention to Cuba once the war in Iran concludes. "We may stop by Cuba after we finish with this," Trump said earlier this week, describing the island as a "failing nation."

item.title: Trump announces Israel-Lebanon ceasefire as oil holds near $95
item.description:
Oil prices moved higher on Thursday as investors weighed a new ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon alongside expectations for a second round of peace talks between the United States and Iran, the two dynamics shaping a conflict that has roiled energy markets for nearly seven weeks.

West Texas Intermediate crude rose more than 2 percent on the day, according to Trading Economics, while Brent crude held near $95 to $97 per barrel. The modest gains came after a volatile stretch that saw prices swing sharply in the aftermath of collapsed negotiations between Washington and Tehran last weekend.

item.title: Pope Leo decries world 'ravaged by tyrants' amid feud with Trump
item.description: Pope Leo XIV delivered some of his most forceful remarks yet on Thursday, declaring that the world is "being ravaged by a handful of tyrants" during a peace gathering in the conflict-scarred city of Bamenda, Cameroon. The address, made at Saint Joseph Cathedral on the second day of his Cameroon visit, came amid an escalating public feud with U.S. President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance over the pontiff's opposition to the war in Iran.

item.title: White House clears path for federal agencies to use Anthropic's Mythos AI
item.description:
The White House Office of Management and Budget is establishing security protocols to allow major federal agencies to begin using Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview, the powerful AI model that has rattled cybersecurity experts and financial regulators on both sides of the Atlantic since its limited release earlier this month. Federal CIO Gregory Barbaccia informed Cabinet departments of the plan, according to a memo reviewed by Bloomberg.

The move comes even as government officials grapple with the model's potential to sharply increase cybersecurity risk — and despite an ongoing legal and political clash between the Trump administration and Anthropic over the use of the company's AI technology.

item.title: Trump says Iran agreed to hand over enriched uranium as deal nears
item.description:
President Donald Trump declared Thursday that Iran has agreed to relinquish its stockpile of enriched uranium, claiming the two sides are "close" to a peace deal to end over six weeks of war. The assertion came as Reuters reported that U.S. and Iranian negotiators have scaled back ambitions for a comprehensive agreement and are instead pursuing a temporary memorandum to prevent a return to hostilities before the ceasefire expires on April 21.

A separate source told Reuters that Iran had agreed to dilute its highly enriched uranium under the supervision of the International Atomic Energy Agency and the United States. A senior Iranian lawmaker, Ali Nikzad, the deputy speaker of parliament, said earlier this week that Tehran had agreed to dilute 450 kilograms of enriched uranium as a goodwill measure, though he added that the United States later backed out of that arrangement.

item.title: IMF says Asia faces worst exposure to Middle East energy shock
item.description: The International Monetary Fund warned on Thursday that Asia is more exposed than any other region to the energy shock unleashed by the war in the Middle East, as the fund's spring meetings in Washington laid bare the widening economic toll of the conflict on the world's poorest nations.

item.title: Israel, Lebanon agree to 10-day ceasefire, Trump says
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced Thursday that Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 10-day ceasefire set to take effect at 5 p.m. EST, pausing weeks of devastating Israeli strikes against Hezbollah that have killed more than 2,000 people in Lebanon since early March.

"These two Leaders have agreed that in order to achieve PEACE between their Countries, they will formally begin a 10 Day CEASEFIRE at 5 P.M. EST," Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that the agreement followed "excellent" conversations with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Trump said he would invite both leaders to the White House for what he called "the first meaningful talks between Israel and Lebanon since 1983." He also said he had directed Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio to work with both countries toward "a Lasting PEACE."
